audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/marktext-bin.git...

Analyzing marktext-bin AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a `source` array using a function `_source()` that is called via command substitution `$(_source)`. This function constructs URLs pointing to the official GitHub repository of marktext (marktext/marktext), specifically to release binaries and static assets like the desktop file and icons. All sources are fetched over HTTPS from github.com, which is the expected and legitimate upstream.

The code executed during sourcing — including the `pkgver` (not present, so default value used) and the `source` array population — involves only string manipulation and URL construction. There is no use of `eval`, `curl|bash`, `wget -O- |`, or any other pattern that would execute downloaded code or exfiltrate data during the sourcing phase. The `sha256sums` array is fully populated with valid checksums, so integrity verification is in place.

While the `prepare()` and `package()` functions contain operations that run later (e.g., `sed`, `cp`, `install`), these are NOT executed during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so they are out of scope for this narrow gate. The only active code during these commands is the top-level sourcing and `_source` function execution, which is safe and limited to fetching verifiable upstream assets.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious code execution during source fetch and parse.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package build process for `marktext-bin`, a precompiled binary release of the Mark Text editor. It fetches assets (binary tarball, desktop file, icons) directly from the official GitHub repository of the project using predictable URLs based on the version tag. All sources are declared in the `_source()` function and included via the `source` array, with fixed SHA-256 checksums provided for each file.

The build process consists of simple and safe operations: patching the desktop file to point to the correct executable path, copying the extracted binary bundle into `/usr/lib`, creating a symlink in `/usr/bin`, installing the desktop entry and icons in their proper system locations, and installing license files. These actions are typical for a `-bin` package and do not involve compilation, dynamic downloads, or execution of external scripts.

There are no signs of malicious behavior such as network exfiltration, obfuscated code, unauthorized file access, or runtime modifications. The use of `sed` to adjust the `Exec` line is standard packaging practice. While the source uses HTTP(S) links to GitHub without pinning to git commits (using release tags instead), this is normal for versioned binary releases and does not constitute a supply-chain risk in this context.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard binary package with no malicious content</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for .nvchecker.toml:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided file `.nvchecker.toml` is a configuration file for nvchecker, a version checking tool commonly used in AUR packages to track upstream releases. The configuration specifies that the version for `marktext-bin` should be checked against GitHub tags from the official repository `marktext/marktext`. It uses a standard tag prefix `v`, applies a regex to match stable version tags (e.g., v1.2.3), and selects the highest tag, which is typical and safe behavior.

There are no network requests, executable commands, or file operations in this file. It does not contain any obfuscated code, suspicious URLs, or data exfiltration mechanisms. The content is purely declarative and within the expected scope of AUR package maintenance tooling. No malicious or risky behavior is present.

This file poses no security risk and aligns with standard practices for version tracking in Arch Linux packaging.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file defines metadata and source locations for the `marktext-bin` package, which is a precompiled binary release of the Mark Text markdown editor. All sources are fetched directly from the official GitHub repository at `https://github.com/marktext/marktext`, specifically from tagged release `v0.19.1`. The URLs use HTTPS, ensuring transport security, and all assets—including the main tarball and desktop/icon files—are pinned to specific paths under this trusted upstream.

Each source has a corresponding `sha256sums` entry, indicating integrity verification is performed during package building. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network requests to third-party hosts. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices: it declares dependencies required by the application, provides and conflicts with `marktext`, and includes necessary desktop integration files. No executable code or build instructions are present in this file—only declarative source and checksum information—which poses no inherent security risk.

While the sources point to mutable refs (e.g., `raw/v0.19.1/...`), they are tied to a fixed tag in a public, auditable repository, and combined with valid checksums, this does not constitute a vulnerability. There is no evidence of injected malicious behavior, data exfiltration, or supply-chain tampering.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard AUR binary package with verified upstream sources and checksums.</summary>
</security_assessment>
